A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a framework for the analysis of TCP congestion avoidance schemes with randomized feedback.

we provide a detailed analysis of the interaction between TCP congestion avoidance and randomized feedback mechanisms such as RED and the ECN marking mechanism, and that we provide a framework for the design of such mechanisms.
we have studied the behavior of TCP congestion avoidance when subjected to randomized feedback, such as ECN and RED.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of ECN as a congestion feedback mechanism is likely to result in a more stable network behavior than the use of RED.
TCP congestion avoidance can be made less sensitive to the randomness of the congestion feedback mechanism.
the use of ECN-based congestion control feedback is not a panacea for the problem of congestion control.
